blocks.text: «Russian verbs may be divided into two basic groups according to their personal endings in the present tense. The present tense has six forms which are used with the corresponding personal pronouns.»
«The 1st type of conjugation is characterized by the vowel **е** (**ё** if accented): the second type is characterized by the vowel **и**.»

«The 1st (or **Е**) type is formed by dropping two last letters from the infinitive and adding personal endings. The 2nd (or **И**) type is formed by dropping three last letters from the infinitive and adding personal endings.»
«The Russian infinitive (such a form as “to read”, “to speak”, “to know”) usually ends in **-ть**. In dictionaries verbs are given in the infinitive.»
From the DLI Grammar Reference Book, Lesson 15, p. 9. · Every form in the tables on this page is the OpenCorpora dictionary's own, generated by tools/courses/gen_tables.py. OpenCorpora, CC BY-SA 4.0.
